slides.content: Cartesian Form of a Plane — Concept
slides.prompt:
Educational mathematics slide, 16:9 widescreen. Dark navy background. Top full-width bold white title bar: 'THE CARTESIAN EQUATION OF A PLANE'. Left 45%: 3D diagram — a translucent teal plane in xyz space. A red arrow labeled 'n = (a, b, c)' points perpendicularly out of the plane (the normal vector). A point P(x, y, z) is marked on the plane surface. The xyz axes are clearly labeled with origin O. Right 55%: white text on slightly lighter navy panel, all text large and fully legible:

THE EQUATION:
ax + by + cz = d

WHERE DOES THIS COME FROM?
The normal vector n = (a, b, c) is perpendicular to every vector that lies IN the plane.

If point A = (x₀, y₀, z₀) is on the plane, and P = (x, y, z) is any point on the plane, then vector AP lies in the plane.

So:  n · AP = 0
→  (a,b,c) · (x−x₀, y−y₀, z−z₀) = 0
→  ax + by + cz = ax₀ + by₀ + cz₀
→  ax + by + cz = d  ✓

KEY INSIGHT:
The normal vector (a, b, c) can be READ directly from the coefficients of x, y, z in the equation.

All text fully legible. Formula in large bold white. Geometric insight in regular weight.

Educational mathematics slide, 16:9 widescreen. Dark navy background. Top full-width bold amber/gold title bar: 'WORKED EXAMPLE — Finding the Cartesian Equation of a Plane'. Full slide content area: white text on dark navy, organized as a step-by-step solution. All text large, clear, fully legible:

QUESTION:
Find the equation of the plane passing through points A(1, 2, 0), B(3, 1, 1) and C(0, 1, 2).

SOLUTION:

Step 1 — Find two vectors lying IN the plane:
  AB = B − A = (3−1, 1−2, 1−0) = (2, −1, 1)
  AC = C − A = (0−1, 1−2, 2−0) = (−1, −1, 2)

Step 2 — Find the normal vector n = AB × AC:
  n = | i   j   k  |
      | 2  −1   1  |
      |−1  −1   2  |

  i: (−1)(2) − (1)(−1) = −2 + 1 = −1
  j: −[(2)(2) − (1)(−1)] = −[4 + 1] = −5
  k: (2)(−1) − (−1)(−1) = −2 − 1 = −3

  n = (−1, −5, −3)  [or equivalently (1, 5, 3)]

Step 3 — Use point A(1, 2, 0) to find d:
  d = 1(1) + 5(2) + 3(0) = 1 + 10 + 0 = 11

ANSWER:  x + 5y + 3z = 11

CHECK: Does B(3,1,1) satisfy it?  3 + 5 + 3 = 11  ✓

All steps clearly numbered. Key results in bold or highlighted box.

slides.content: Scalar Product Form r·n = p — Concept
slides.prompt:
Educational mathematics slide, 16:9 widescreen. Dark navy background. Top full-width bold white title bar: 'SCALAR PRODUCT FORM:  r · n = p'. Left 45%: 3D diagram — translucent teal plane. Origin O shown. A position vector r drawn from O to a general point P on the plane (orange arrow). Normal vector n pointing out of the plane (red arrow). A point A on the plane shown with position vector a. The angle between r and n is illustrated with a dotted arc. Right 55%: white text fully legible:

THE EQUATION:
r · n = p

WHERE DOES THIS COME FROM?
Let A be a known point on the plane with position vector a.
Let P be any point on the plane with position vector r.

Then AP = r − a lies IN the plane.
Since n is perpendicular to everything in the plane:
  n · (r − a) = 0
  n · r − n · a = 0
  r · n = n · a

So:  p = n · a  (a constant — just compute it!)

CONNECTION TO CARTESIAN FORM:
If n = (a, b, c) and r = (x, y, z) then:
  r · n = ax + by + cz
So  r · n = p  is exactly the same as  ax + by + cz = p  ✓

They are the SAME equation, written differently.

All text and formulas large, fully legible, white on dark navy.

Educational mathematics slide, 16:9 widescreen. Dark navy background. Top full-width bold amber/gold title bar: 'WORKED EXAMPLE — Converting Between Forms'. Full content area: clear step-by-step solution, all text large and fully legible in white:

QUESTION:
The plane Π has equation  r · (2, −1, 3) = 7.
(a) Write Π in Cartesian form.
(b) Show that the point A(1, −1, 2) lies on Π.
(c) Find a unit normal to Π.

SOLUTION:

(a) Expand r · n with r = (x, y, z) and n = (2, −1, 3):
    2x − y + 3z = 7
    This IS the Cartesian form.  ✓

(b) Substitute A(1, −1, 2) into 2x − y + 3z:
    2(1) − (−1) + 3(2) = 2 + 1 + 6 = 9 ≠ 7

    Wait — A does NOT lie on Π. Let us instead check B(3, 2, 0):
    2(3) − (2) + 3(0) = 6 − 2 + 0 = 4 ≠ 7

    Check C(1, 0, 5/3):  2(1) − 0 + 3(5/3) = 2 + 5 = 7  ✓  C lies on Π.

(c) Unit normal  n̂ = n / |n|:
    |n| = √(2² + (−1)² + 3²) = √(4 + 1 + 9) = √14
    n̂ = (2/√14,  −1/√14,  3/√14)

All working shown. Boxed final answers. Steps numbered clearly.

slides.content: Parametric Vector Form r = a + λb + μc — Concept
slides.prompt:
Educational mathematics slide, 16:9 widescreen. Dark navy background. Top full-width bold white title bar: 'PARAMETRIC VECTOR FORM:  r = a + λb + μc'. Left 45%: 3D diagram — a translucent teal plane. A specific point A on the plane marked with position vector a (yellow arrow from origin O). Two direction vectors b (blue arrow) and c (green arrow) lying WITHIN the plane surface, originating from A. A general point P on the plane shown, with the path a + λb + μc illustrated by dashed arrows. Right 55%: white text fully legible:

THE EQUATION:
r = a + λb + μc
(λ, μ are free real-number parameters)

HOW TO READ IT:
• a = position vector of a known point on the plane
• b, c = two non-parallel direction vectors that lie IN the plane
• By varying λ and μ over all real values, r sweeps out the ENTIRE plane

WHY DOES IT WORK?
Any point in the plane can be reached from A by moving some amount in the b direction and some amount in the c direction — just like a 2D coordinate system, but embedded in 3D space.

FINDING b AND c IN PRACTICE:
If you know three points A, B, C on the plane:
  b = AB = B − A
  c = AC = C − A

CONVERTING TO CARTESIAN:
Find n = b × c (normal vector), then use n · (r − a) = 0.

All text and diagram labels large and fully legible.

Educational mathematics slide, 16:9 widescreen. Dark navy background. Top full-width bold amber/gold title bar: 'WORKED EXAMPLE — Using the Parametric Form'. Full content area: step-by-step solution, all text large, clear, fully legible in white on dark navy:

QUESTION:
A plane passes through A(2, 0, 1) and contains the direction vectors b = (1, 1, 0) and c = (0, 1, 2).
(a) Write the equation of the plane in parametric vector form.
(b) Find whether the point Q(4, 3, 3) lies on the plane.
(c) Convert to Cartesian form.

SOLUTION:

(a) Parametric form directly:
    r = (2, 0, 1) + λ(1, 1, 0) + μ(0, 1, 2)

(b) Test Q(4, 3, 3): We need λ and μ such that:
    2 + λ = 4     →  λ = 2
    0 + λ + μ = 3  →  2 + μ = 3  →  μ = 1
    1 + 0 + 2μ = 3  →  1 + 2 = 3  ✓

    All three equations are satisfied with λ=2, μ=1.
    Therefore Q DOES lie on the plane.  ✓

(c) Convert to Cartesian — find n = b × c:
    n = (1,1,0) × (0,1,2)
    = ( 1·2 − 0·1,  0·0 − 1·2,  1·1 − 1·0 )
    = (2, −2, 1)

    d = n · a = (2)(2) + (−2)(0) + (1)(1) = 5

    Cartesian form:  2x − 2y + z = 5

    Check Q(4,3,3):  8 − 6 + 3 = 5  ✓

All steps legible. Final answers in bold or highlighted.

Educational mathematics slide, 16:9 widescreen. Dark navy background. Top full-width bold white title bar: 'THE VECTOR PRODUCT  a × b'. Left 45%: 3D diagram — two vectors a (orange/amber arrow) and b (yellow arrow) originating from the same point, with the angle θ clearly labeled between them using a curved arc. A bright green arrow labeled 'a × b' shoots perpendicularly upward from the same origin, illustrating the right-hand rule. Dotted reference lines show the parallelogram formed by a and b. A shaded parallelogram area is filled in light teal. Small right-angle box at the base of a × b to show perpendicularity. Right 55%: white text fully legible:

DEFINITION — MAGNITUDE:
|a × b| = |a||b| sin θ
where θ is the angle between a and b  (0 ≤ θ ≤ π)

DIRECTION — Right-Hand Rule:
Point fingers along a, curl toward b → thumb points in direction of a × b

COMPONENT FORMULA:
a × b = ( a₂b₃ − a₃b₂ )
        ( a₃b₁ − a₁b₃ )
        ( a₁b₂ − a₂b₁ )

KEY PROPERTIES:
• a × b is perpendicular to BOTH a and b
• a × b = −(b × a)   [anti-commutative]
• a × a = 0
• a × b = 0  ⟺  a and b are parallel
• |a × b| = area of parallelogram formed by a and b

GEOMETRIC MEANING:
|a × b| is largest when a ⊥ b (sin 90° = 1)
|a × b| = 0 when a ∥ b (sin 0° = 0)

All formulas and labels large, fully legible, white text.
